overall_why: I would use three.js again for a similar game. The work an agent can actually finish — seeded rules, a script-controlled clock, save dumps, and real HTML controls — stayed ordinary JavaScript, and the WebGL view stayed out of the way: headless Chromium ran the full proof twice with the same frame times, and about a thousand plants were still a few milliseconds. A 3D sim is mostly a picture, though, and that part was a silent loop. Physical lights made the first meadow nearly black, the glTF face and the barrel's vertex colors did not match the art notes, and the only signal was another screenshot. Survivable, and it was the whole tax.
